### Real results

A former valet earned over $85K doing work he'd been doing as a passion project. He owns the company.

An employee who lost everything caring for his late wife earned 2× median household income and moved his new family into a home on acreage. He owns the company.

Our companies absorbed two struggling businesses, protected their investors, retained most employees, and generated $336K in earnings for four principals. They own the company.

The thesis

## The data is not subtle.

Exposure to private business interests is the primary driver of long-term wealth creation. Labor is a commodity — motivated talent is not. People have never been more productive, and the ones with real skin in the game are more productive still. The evidence has accumulated for decades and it all points in one direction.

On employee ownership

Incentive alignment works. It has always worked. A person who owns what they build behaves differently from a person who is paid to maintain it. The research — from academic institutions, institutional investors, and the federal government — says the same thing. Ownership changes behavior. Behavior changes results.

—FCLT GlobalLong-term ownership mindset drives higher capital returns

—HRMJEmployee ownership correlates with sustained organizational performance

—Ownership Works$1.7B+ distributed to 100,000+ frontline workers across 90+ companies

—National Center for Employee Ownership30,000+ ESOPs in the U.S. — the model scales

—UPenn / WhartonBroad-based equity improves firm outcomes on every major metric

—GAO (1987)Congress's auditing arm validated the model before it was fashionable — the 1987 report is oft-cited but not fully digitized

On fund size

J.P. Morgan and PitchBook analyzed 1,690 private equity funds across two decades. The finding is unambiguous: first-quartile performance is overwhelmingly concentrated at small fund sizes. Above $10B, it nearly disappears. We are deliberately small, and we intend to stay that way.

About Us — nth Venture Inc.

# About Us.

### Setting talented people free through the power of ownership.

nth Venture was founded in November 2021 with this simple mission that drives us forward.

### Discovering our “Why”.

Most of us have at some point in our career said, “why am I doing this?” One of the great luxuries at nth Venture is that we don’t have to avoid that question in a cynical bid to improve turnover. It’s front and center for us. At the onset, we make sure people have an answer so strong they’ll never forget it.

## Studio Process

## Step 1.

### White Space Design.

This is where we start our business-building journey, laying out a map of the challenges, solutions, talent, products and services as well as a finalized initial target market for each unit. One of many learning stages in our build process, the white space design period is for identifying and answering hard questions that will shape the business.

## Step 2.

### Dry Dock Build.

In this stage, the build begins and we create the brand, platforms, products, prototypes, services, team and process design to hit the market ahead and course-correct on any aspects that may need adjustment prior to the test stage.

## Step 3.

### Wet Dock Test.

With the initial build work now complete, we bring our prototype to the market with a soft launch, testing our hypothesis, and tightening up processes and operational readiness ahead of launch. This is a time for refinement, enhancements and adding polish.

## Step 4.

### Anchor Up Launch.

We launch our businesses and teams with tested and realistic routes to market, with a clear vision and mission including the support, guidance and communication needed to succeed.

## Step 5.

### Operating Fleet.

Once the business launches out of the studio, it joins our operating fleet, where it has the continued support of the nth Venture studio and proven model to succeed on its journey.

 "

## Killing the J Curve.

The J Curve is what’s taught in most educational and mainstream entrepreneurship courses today as gospel when it comes to starting new ventures. Hear how at nth Venture we are bending the J curve from our very own CEO Sam Sawhook.

## Building together.

## Ownership for everyone drives value for everyone.

#### Audily

### Building resilient and profit-driven businesses.

Audily President Matt Wells discusses the value of launching Audily, the studio experience, continued support, and the future of the Podcast and audiobook production industry.

Visit Audily ➜

## Profit-Sharing & Equity Comp

Our purpose is simple: Set talented people free through the power of ownership.

nth Venture’s deep alignment philosophy allows us to build sustainable, disciplined businesses and reliably place world-class talent.

Both in the studio and in our ventures, we unapologetically align incentives through profit-sharing and equity.

The academic literature is crystal clear when it comes to incentive alignment and we’re a living example of it. We’re just a little more radical in how we apply it.

The result is all our people are intensely focused on organizational performance in ways that drive long-term value and minimize early costs.

The combination of our unique, inertia-overcoming compensation structure with a seasoned studio staff and launch process has created a value-generation machine with our goal of widespread ownership at the heart.

It means true skin in the game, no your matter your level in the organization.

Whiteboarding with Sam, our CEO ➜

## Building For Forever

"Sam and the team have created a special sauce for building innovative new businesses." - David Wan

Retired Chairman & CEO

We don’t give tips and hold happy hours. We’re hands-on builders.

We start with ideas generated internally by the studio team, find the very best executives in the world to build them out, and spend six months supporting them as they build out an organic growth machine business.

#### Merchant Boxes

### Moving and growing faster with nth Venture.

Merchant Boxes President Doug Epperly discusses the value of launching Merchant Boxes, the studio experience, continued support, and the future of the packaging industry.

Visit Merchant Boxes ➜

## Why It Works

Strong Bias to Autonomy

Our incentive structure means we get to spend less time managing performance and more time building. Our teams work where, when, and on what makes sense. People deserve ownership not only in the places they work, but of their lives. We make certain they get both here.

Radical Incentive Alignment

We believe that tying pay to hours worked is an unfortunate vestige of the industrial revolution that isn’t a great fit for the modern working world. By compensating our people on a profit-sharing basis we unlock the extraordinary power of durable, high-performance teams.

Effective Support

We provide a top-flight working platform for great talent so they can focus on doing their life’s best work and build businesses that make an impact. Our functional support and shared services give our ventures more bandwidth to focus on being exceptional in their field.

## Our Investment Philosophy

Our disciplined approach is centered around the exceptionally clear results of decades of academic work and practicing exemplars like Berkshire Hathaway, Markel and DFA.

Invest for the long-term,

avoid fees,

ensure proper – but not excessive – diversification

in simple businesses with

passionate, effective and high-integrity managers.

We apply those principles in the studio to cultivate a portfolio of strong, resilient companies where people can work long-term and see the fruits of their labor.
